title: Package of Practices for Rice Cultivation in India
source: ICAR - National Rice Research Institute (NRRI), Cuttack
content: Rice (Oryza sativa) requires deep, clayey or loamy soils rich in organic matter with slightly acidic to neutral pH (5.5 to 7.0). For land preparation in wet nursery (transplanted puddle rice), puddle the soil thoroughly by 2-3 plowings in 5-10 cm standing water followed by leveling using a wooden plank to reduce water percolation. Seed rate for transplanted rice: 35-40 kg/ha for coarse varieties, 30-35 kg/ha for medium/fine grains, and 15-20 kg/ha for hybrids. Treat seeds with Carbendazim 2g/kg seed or bio-fungicide Trichoderma viride 5g/kg seed before sowing. Nursery management: Sow sprouted seeds in wet nursery bed (10 cents per hectare of main field). Seedlings are ready for transplanting at 21-25 days (4-leaf stage). Spacing: Maintain 20 cm x 15 cm (hill spacing) with 2-3 seedlings per hill. For System of Rice Intensification (SRI), transplant 8-12 day old single seedlings at 25 cm x 25 cm spacing. Weed control: Apply Pre-emergence herbicide Pretilachlor 50 EC @ 1.0 kg a.i./ha at 3-5 days after transplanting (DAT) or perform conoweeder operations at 15 and 30 DAT. Maintain shallow water (2-3 cm) during early vegetative phase.
